pk.context: 45 mg oral, single dose, healthy adults

clues.kinetics: No clinically significant food effect was seen with a high-calorie, high-fat meal. It is 51% bound to plasma proteins and primarily metabolized by CYP1A2, with 76.9% of the dose excreted in urine.
clues.substance: A small molecule that is a white powder, very slightly soluble in water at 0.29 mg/mL, with a molecular weight of 358.39.
clues.product: Approved under an NDA in one strength only, dosed once daily.
clues.safety: Boxed warning for hepatotoxicity; contraindicated with known cirrhosis, severe renal impairment or end-stage renal disease, and CYP1A2 inhibitors. Abdominal pain and diarrhea are the most common reactions.
clues.indication: Treats moderate to severe vasomotor symptoms due to menopause.
clues.mechanism: Blocks the neurokinin 3 (NK3) receptor, so neurokinin B cannot act in the thermoregulatory center. Affinity for NK3 is more than 450-fold higher than for NK1 or NK2.

tell: A boxed hepatotoxicity warning and CYP1A2-dependent clearance set this NK3 receptor antagonist apart.
